models.name: Gemma 4 E2B
models.why: Gemma 4 E2B on a Raspberry Pi 5 through LiteRT-LM: the decode figure is once again 9 tokens/sec, with the 1432 MB peak RAM and the 99 tok/s prefill stated in the same post.

engines.quant: Gemma 4 E2B through LiteRT-LM; 99 tok/s prefill; tokenizer ~4.2 chars/token; VideoCore VII GPU kept for vision/audio so the CPU stays free for the LLM

models.name: DeepSeek-R1 1.5B
models.why: A 7-year-old Raspberry Pi 4B with 2GB of RAM serving DeepSeek R1 1.5B offline at 4 tokens/sec on a 5W budget — the CPU-only floor of what still answers.

engines.hardware: Raspberry Pi 4B, 2GB LPDDR4, ARM CPU only
engines.quant: boots Ollama on the Pi and serves DeepSeek R1 1.5B quantized; no internet required; ~5W under load

models.name: Gemma 3 1B
models.full_name: Gemma 3 1B (Q4_K_M, llama.cpp on a Raspberry Pi 4)
models.why: Trelis Research's CPU-only Pi 4 baseline: Gemma 3 1B Q4_K_M decodes at 2.9 tok/s and Gemma 4 E2B at 1.0 — the honest numbers for voice agents on a Pi.

engines.hardware: Raspberry Pi 4 (Cortex-A72, 4 cores, 8GB RAM), CPU-only ARMv8.0
engines.quant: Gemma 3 1B Q4_K_M (769 MB); prompt 5.9 t/s, gen 2.9 t/s
